recheck.evidence_quote: Starter: Max connections 5, Monthly tier fee "No charge", Payment method "Not applicable", Prerequisites "None", rate limit 1000 per day per org.
recheck.notes: Verified on Xero's own pages (developer.xero.com/pricing and /faq/pricing-and-policy-updates): Starter tier is free, needs no payment method or prerequisites, with 5 connections max and 1,000 calls/day/org. The FAQ says Starter gives "unlimited data access to enable early innovation", so normal data pulls are allowed within those caps. Paid tiers (AUD, excl. tax): Core $35/mo for 50 connections, 10 GB egress; Plus $245 for 1,000 connections, needs App Certification; Advanced $1,445 for 10,000 connections, needs App Certification plus a security assessment; Enterprise is price on application. Overage is $2.40/GB. Core and above need a credit card, with 5,000 calls/day/org. Shared limits: 5 concurrent, 60/min per org, 10,000/min per app. Journals, XPM and Bulk Connections are premium and need security assessment and use-case approval. The page extract was ambiguous on which tiers include them, so that is unconfirmed. Custom Connections: the FAQ says they "remain on the same commercial terms" and sit outside the new pricing model, but it gives no price. The ~US$5/month figure is still unverified. API style: Xero's GitHub org (XeroAPI/Xero-OpenAPI) publishes OpenAPI 3.0 specs, so REST. Specs cover Accounting, Identity, Bank Feeds, Fixed Assets, Project, Payroll AU/UK/NZ and Files. I did not find GraphQL or SOAP. Not verified: the OAuth2 docs page did not render, so the grant types (auth code, PKCE, client credentials) are not confirmed from Xero's own OAuth docs. /llms.txt returned 404. The 'official' MCP status is still inferred from the XeroAPI org. One search snippet said the pricing pages are about a year old, so recheck the live page before relying on the exact fees.
